stories.title: Who is Alice Huang, the Chinese executive accused of spying on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang?
summary: Tech executive Alice Huang is the woman accused of spying for China during an affair with Jensen Huang, head of US artificial intelligence chip titan Nvidia, according to media reports.

Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen recruited by Beijing to collect intelligence on the Nvidia boss, according to The New York Times, which first reported that Jensen Huang was the alleged target of a spy plot.
At the time, Alice Huang was said to be a top executive at data centre firm Megaspeed International, which rents out computing power to other companies to train and run AI.

stories.title: Punjab CM says those who 'raise their hand against a helpless woman' will suffer the same fate
summary: Her comments came in response a video of a man physically assaulting a sales girl at Kohinoor Plaza in Faisalabad.
Police said the “enraged” man then physically assaulted the girl, with CCTV footage showing him yanking her from behind the counter and eventually throwing her to the ground.
Last month, CM Maryam also took notice of a man who physically assaulted a woman riding a scooty on Mozang Ring Road in Lahore.

stories.title: UK's Russell Brand sentenced to 10-and-a-half years in jail for rape, sexual assault
summary: Comedian Russell Brand, once one of Britain’s most high-profile broadcasters and a Hollywood star, was jailed for 10-and-a-half years on Monday after he was convicted of raping one woman and sexually assaulting three more around two decades ago.

Brand — the former husband of US pop singer Katy Perry who in recent years moved away from the mainstream — was convicted on Thursday of raping one woman and sexually assaulting three more between 2004 and 2009.
Brand, who starred in films such as “Forgetting Sarah Marshall”, “Get Him to the Greek” and “Arthur”, had denied ever having non-consensual sex.

stories.title: Team formed to probe suspected targeted killing of Karachi inspector Javed Abro
summary: KARACHI: A high-level police team has been formed to probe the suspected targeted killing of inspector Javed Abro, who was gunned down by armed pillion riders in Karachi’s Steel Town a day earlier, officials said on Monday.
Karachi Additional Inspector General (AIG) Azad Khan told Dawn that an investigation team headed by the Malir senior superintendent of police (SSP) has been constituted.
Hammad, a son of Abro, said police personnel had been deployed for the former SHO’s security, but his father had sent them on leave around a week ago.

stories.title: Trump says 'great dislike' for Israel contributed to Republican rout in midterms
summary: Separately, he also cast doubt on renewed fighting with Iran, telling CNN it was “highly unlikely”.

The president told CNN in an interview on Sunday that renewed fighting was “highly unlikely,” but warned that his decision “depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement.” “I would if necessary, but we hit them really hard.

So has our region.” In Sunday’s CNN interview, Trump once again suggested that the economic pressure Iran is under will force its leaders into accepting the United States’ terms. “They’re a failing nation.

stories.title: Pakistan condemns targeting of Aramco building, demands Houthis cease all attacks against Saudi Arabia
summary: Pakistan on Monday condemned the Houthi attack on Saudi oil giant Aramco’s corporate office in Riyadh, demanding that the rebel group “immediately and unconditionally” cease all attacks against Saudi Arabia, the Foreign Office (FO) said.
On Sunday, an Aramco building in Riyadh was tar­geted in an “attempted attack”, the Saudi energy ministry said, which damaged the skyscraper.

Expressing solidarity with Saudi Arabia, the statement added that Pakistan stood resolutely with the leadership of the kingdom and “reaffirm our full support for all measures necessary to safeguard its security, sovereignty and territorial integrity”.

stories.title: Lahore remains world’s most polluted major city as AQI crosses 600
summary: The deterioration came a day after the Punjab government warned that smoke from Diwali fireworks in neighbouring Indian Punjab, crop-residue burning and easterly winds could aggravate air pollution in Lahore and adjoining districts.
It forecast an increase in pollution levels in Lahore, Kasur and border areas on the morning of Nov 9, as easterly winds were expected to carry polluted air from Indian territory towards Pakistan.
Air pollution worsened by agri fires The Punjab government’s report recorded 2,347 incidents of crop-residue burning in Indian Punjab up to Nov 4.

stories.title: Sialkot police arrest TikToker for allegedly threatening family of stampede victim
summary: NAROWAL: Sialkot police said on Monday they have arrested TikToker Muhammad Ansar Jatt, alias “Mr Pattlo”, for allegedly threatening the family of a man who died in a stampede at an event in connection with his wedding.

Subsequently, a first information report (FIR) was registered at the Motra Police Station, naming Jatt, his brother, the owner of Faraz Cricket Ground, six others, and 40-45 unidentified security guards.

Abu Bakr claimed that on his intervention, two unknown persons took out their pistols and aimed them at him, threatening to kill him and the family members if they did not reach a peaceful settlement with Jatt and his brother.

stories.title: TV anchor's killing: Rawalpindi court grants police one-day physical remand of victim's husband
summary: RAWALPINDI: A local court on Monday granted police one-day physical remand of Ahsan, the husband of anchorperson Rabia Ahsan, who was shot dead at home in the Gulshanabad area a day earlier.
On Monday, the suspect was presented before Area Magistrate Talat Waheed by police, who sought seven days of physical custody for further investigation.

After hearing the police request, the magistrate approved one day of physical remand of the suspect, allowing investigators to interrogate him and pursue further investigation into the circumstances surrounding the anchorperson’s death.

stories.title: Bangladesh challenges ousted PM Hasina to seek extradition as she requests new passport
summary: Bangladesh challenged on Monday ousted leader Sheikh Hasina to seek extradition from India if she was serious about returning home, while reviewing an application to renew her passport.

Hasina, whose 15-year rule was ended by a mass uprising she tried to crush, has vowed to return in December to Bangladesh, where she was sentenced to death for crimes against humanity over the 2024 crackdown on protesters.

Dhaka police spokesman Md Akhtar Hossain said the suspects were members of Hasina’s banned Awami League party. “They are trying to create panic among people,” he told AFP. “We are remaining vigilant to deal with any untoward situation.”

stories.title: Pakistan post 281-5 to punish Sri Lanka in first Test
summary: Captain Babar Azam and two debutants were among four batters to hit half-centuries as Pakistan reached 281-5 on day one of the first Test against Sri Lanka on Monday.

Opener Tayyab Arif scored an impressive 57 and Mohammad Taha a patient 51 — both playing their first Test — while Azam hit 50, with Sri Lanka’s decision to bowl on what appeared to be a green pitch in Rawalpindi seemed to backfire.
Sri Lanka’s decision to go with a pace quartet and without a frontline spinner could also prove costly, with the pitch not offering much to the fast bowlers.

stories.title: Pakistani farmers in long fight to make German firms pay for 2022 flood damage
summary: The companies are being targeted not over specific operations in Pakistan, but because of their climate-warming emissions.
Heidelberg Materials told AFP its operations were compliant with German laws and that firms could not be expected to retroactively face different standards.

Even if the case succeeds, an uphill battle remains for millions across Pakistan, ranked among the countries most affected by climate change despite contributing less than one per cent of global emissions.

stories.title: Nvidia probes whether CEO Huang was target of foreign spying as he admits affair
summary: Nvidia said on Monday its board was probing whether CEO Jensen Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, after a media report alleged he had a close relationship with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to Beijing.

Huang said in a message to employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife and took “full responsibility” for his actions, while Nvidia said the CEO was committed to continuing to lead the company without interruption.
The board has confidence in the CEO and his leadership team, Nvidia said, adding that Huang fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it.

stories.title: 'I stand with my brother': David Warner says Usman Khawaja's 'sandpapergate' claims '100pc accurate'
summary: Warner, one of three players banned over the ball-tampering controversy in Cape Town along with Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft, said he stood “with my brother” Khawaja. “It’s been eight years since I spoke on this topic,” the former opener said on Instagram.
Cricket Australia’s original investigation found only Smith, Warner and Bancroft were in the know, with the governing body at the weekend saying it remained “comfortable” with its findings.

I stand with my brother Usman Khawaja. “Speaking your truth takes courage, especially when people would rather you stay silent. “Time passing doesn’t replace accountability, and asking questions shouldn’t be mistaken for holding grudges.

stories.title: Water surges into nearby work areas after rock mass collapse at Tarbela Dam
summary: SWABI: A rock mass collapsed at the Tarbela Dam 5th Extension Project (T-5) construction site on Monday, causing a surge of water to enter nearby work areas, said the Water and Power Development Authority (Wapda).

In a statement, Wapda said that water entered the under-construction power house area and a tunnel of the T-5 project after a weak rock mass collapsed during excavation work, prompting the evacuation of workers.

Authorities were assessing whether the tunnel, power house and other structures in the working area had sustained any damage, Deputy Commissioner Haripur Waseem Ahmed said, quoting officials of the T-5 project.

stories.title: COP31 opens with leaders under pressure to tackle climate crisis
summary: Inventor said developed countries were “taking a hard line” over whether to include a platform, agreed at COP30 in Brazil last year, aimed at discussing how wealthy nations should provide funds to developing nations.
Countries committed to transition away from fossil fuels in a landmark pact at COP28 in Dubai in 2023 but have struggled to agree on how to turn that pledge into action.
COP30 ended with a deal that made no explicit mention of fossil fuels after oil-producing countries opposed the language.

stories.title: Rabid Modi
summary: IN Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s India, minorities are cast as either infiltrators or in-house enemies.
India Hate Lab has recorded 60 incidents of vandalism and assaults on pastors and prayer congregations on the pretext of illegal conversions since the BJP took power in West Bengal.

The UN Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination advised India to address hate speech, discrimination, and hate crimes, refrain from hounding Rohingya, Bengali Muslims, and migrants, and respect freedoms.

stories.title: Opposition alliance hints at movement against govt, hopes JUI-F chief will lead the effort
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Tehreek Tahafuz-i-Ayeen Pakistan (TTAP) on Monday hinted at starting a movement against the incumbent government, with hopes that Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman may lead it.
Last week, opposition leaders and JUI-F agreed to strengthen their alliance and parliamentary coordination amid recent tensions between the latter and the federal government.
Fazl has been critical of the federal government over the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

stories.title: Drap urges public to verify authenticity and prices of medicines via new app
summary: About 800 pharmaceutical companies and more than 90,000 medicines were registered with Drap, Sajid Shah, a spokesperson for the Ministry of National Health Services, told Dawn.
Shah said Drap had set up a 2D barcode system that allows consumers to scan medicine packs and ensure they receive safe, high-quality and effective products.
Earlier this year, Drap had set October 1 as the cut-off date for launching the barcode system to curb the sale of counterfeit and expired medicines and eradicate black marketing.

stories.title: PM directs foreign ministry to urgently ‘escalate humanitarian assistance’ for rain-hit Gaza
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said on Monday he had directed the foreign ministry to pursue all possible means to urgently “escalate humanitarian assistance” to Gaza, where heavy rains have flooded tens of thousands of tents housing displaced Palestinians.

The Gaza government media office said on Sunday that at least 70,000 tents had been flooded in the past 12 hours, affecting tens of thousands of displaced people and causing injuries, although no fatalities had been reported.
Palestinian authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed in Gaza since Israel began its assault on the territory.

stories.title: Pakistan condemns Houthi attack on Saudi Aramco building, denounces targeting of civilian facilities
summary: Pakistan on Monday condemned the attempted attack by the Houthis on a Saudi Aramco building in Riyadh, while expressing concern over the targeting of civilian facilities.

An attack claimed by Yemen's Houthis damaged Saudi Aramco's corporate tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District on Sunday, shattering windows across several floors and marking a further escalation in the conflict between the group and the kingdom.
In a statement on X, the Foreign Office (FO) said: "Pakistan strongly condemns the attempted attack by the Houthis on a Saudi Aramco administrative building in Riyadh.

stories.title: Security forces neutralise terrorists’ hideouts in North Waziristan’s Mir Ali: ISPR
summary: Security forces conducted an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Muzak village, on the southern outskirts of Mir Ali in North Waziristan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, neutralising two terrorist hideouts, the military’s media wing said on Monday.
Meanwhile, KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi described the incident as “deeply distressing” while also praising the security forces for the successful IBO, Pakistan TV reported.
On October 8, security forces killed nine terrorists in an IBO in North Waziristan, while a day earlier, 18 terrorists were eliminated in separate engagements in KP and Balochistan.

stories.title: President, PM say Iqbal’s vision continues to serve as a 'guiding beacon' for Pakistan
summary: It was at the Allahabad session of the Muslim League in 1930 that Iqbal became the first politician to articulate the two-nation theory that ultimately led to the creation of Pakistan on August 14, 1947.
His poetry also spoke to a wider human struggle: the pursuit of freedom, equality and a life of self-respect,” a statement issued by the president’s office quoted him as saying.

President Zardari stressed that Iqbal’s vision called to “build a Pakistan where the worker receives a fair wage, the farmer enjoys the fruits of his labour, and every child can learn and advance, regardless of family circumstances, gender or faith”.

stories.title: Trump calls Nvidia's Huang 'honorable,' says he has not discussed allegations with him
summary: US President Donald Trump on Sunday called Nvidia ​CEO Jensen Huang an honorable person ‌and praised his contributions to the United States, but said he had not spoken to him ​about allegations of a relationship with ​a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to ⁠Beijing.
I just know he's a ​fine person, but you never know what is going on," Trump told reporters.
When asked if he would take Huang on his ⁠trip ​to Asia next week, ​Trump said: "I don't know, but I'd certainly take him."

stories.title: Trump says he was 'only kidding' about naming UFC CEO as White House press secretary
summary: In Saturday’s post, Trump described White as a “violent Fighter and Warrior” and suggested he bring several current or former UFC champions to serve as assistants, saying they were needed to “defend us against the Lunatic Left”.
White, who has led the UFC for more than two decades, has been a close Trump ally and helped mobilise support for his 2024 presidential campaign.
He has also appeared alongside Trump at several political events and helped bring UFC fights to the White House lawn this year.

stories.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia investors launch fund to boost trade, investment
summary: The Saudi-Pakistan Joint ⁠Business Council (SPJBC), formed by ​the governments of both countries, said ​the fund's initial size was "multi-hundred million", which was expected to expand based ​on opportunities across sectors.
Earlier in October, SPJBC Chairman Prince Mansour bin Mohammad Al Saud visited Pakistan, leading a high-level Saudi business delegation.

Read: Pakistan eyes strategic economic ties with KSA: PM Before that, in August, a high-level Saudi business delegation, led by the SPJBC chairman, called on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif at the PM House, according to a statement issued by the government.

stories.title: COP31 summit leaders urge world to move faster on climate
summary: Leaders of the COP31 climate summit urged the world to accelerate the fight against ​global warming amid rising temperatures and worsening climate-driven disasters, as the annual meeting began in Turkey on Monday.
Turkey's COP31 presidency has ​focused this year's summit on a goal to electrify more than a third of the global economy by 2035, up from around a fifth today.

"We want people to feel the results of climate talks in daily life: in buildings that use less energy, in clean public transport, in energy they can afford and in new jobs," Turkey's COP31 President Murat Kurum said.

stories.title: Tesla to refund many Cybertruck deposits as demand exceeds production, Musk says
summary: Tesla will have to refund Cybertruck deposits for ​many customers as orders far exceed production capacity, CEO ‌Elon Musk said, following last week's announcement that the electric vehicle maker is winding down the pickup ​truck's production at its Texas factory.
The Cybertruck order rate far exceeds our production rate.
We will try to make as many as possible before shutting down the line in about 8 months, but will have to return deposits for a lot of people.

stories.title: Hina Altaf shares uncomfortable experience during flight, calls out man for repeatedly staring at her
summary: Pakistani actress Hina Altaf took to her Instagram stories to share an uncomfortable experience she allegedly encountered while travelling on a flight.
The actress posted a video of a fellow male passenger whom she accused of repeatedly staring at her during the journey, expressing her displeasure over his behaviour.
Altaf is a well-known Pakistani television actress, presenter and former video jockey.

stories.title: Mahira Khan shares message on how women are treated during pregnancy and postpartum
summary: Pakistani actor Mahira Khan drew attention to the importance of treating women with kindness and compassion during pregnancy and the postpartum period through a thought-provoking message.

Although Mahira did not identify anyone or elaborate on the message, her Instagram story has brought renewed attention to the emotional support and understanding women need while navigating pregnancy and life after childbirth.

With her latest Instagram story, Mahira has highlighted a conversation that extends beyond pregnancy itself: the importance of how women are treated, supported and remembered during a particularly vulnerable chapter of their lives.

stories.title: Saud steadies Pakistan’s innings
summary: Saud remained unbeaten on 57 off 112 deliveries, clobbering seven fours, while wicket-keeper batsman Ghazi Ghori was not out on seven when bad light forced an early end to the proceedings after 67.2 overs.
Tayyab continued with attacking approach and brought up his first fifty on debut off just 46 deliveries, including nine fours and a six.
The pair took Pakistan to 159 before Babar departed for 50 off 58 deliveries, having struck seven fours.

stories.title: Durefishan Saleem tells fans to respect Zaryab’s choice as ‘Dar-e-Nijaat’ sparks clothing debate
summary: Durefishan Saleem has a message for those questioning Zaryab's latest clothing decision in Dar-e-Nijaat: a woman's right to choose what she wears must extend in every direction.

Making it clear that the character's choice was neither imposed by her husband Abu Bakr nor a declaration about how other women should dress, Saleem emphasised that it was simply part of Zaryab's personal journey.

Acknowledging that viewers are entitled to their own interpretations of the character, Saleem said audiences could look at Zaryab's choices through their own moral lens, disagree with them or question their timing.

stories.title: US military preparations underway near Gaza border for international force deployment: Israeli media
summary: United States military preparations are underway near the Gaza Strip border ahead of the planned deployment of an international stabilisation force inside the Palestinian enclave, Israeli media reported Monday.

US preparations According to Walla, US troops and officers from other countries have recently been seen near the Gaza border, while an Israeli military base in the south has been converted into a secured US facility.

The US military has also transferred vehicles and military equipment to a designated base within the area of responsibility of the Israeli army’s Southern Brigade of the Gaza Division, near the border, according to Walla.

stories.title: China extends US trade truce by two months
summary: China on Monday effectively extended its trade truce with the United States by two months, after announcing it would continue to suspend certain trade measures.
It added that measures affecting 11 US firms on China's unreliable entities list and 16 on its export control list will remain suspended through to January 10, 2027.

The suspension of special port fees on US-linked vessels will be extended until January 10, 2027, China's transport ministry said, adding that a probe into shipping and shipbuilding supply chain security will remain suspended.

stories.title: Demarcation begins to clear Peshawar's University Road of encroachments
summary: PESHAWAR: The district administration has begun demarcating encroachments along University Road here to prepare for a major operation aimed at clearing the busy thoroughfare and improving traffic flow.

Officials will launch the operation after completing the demarcation process to remove encroachments on both sides of the road to widen the thoroughfare, facilitate its reconstruction and remove obstacles to smooth traffic movement.
University Road is one of the city’s major arteries, where encroachments have frequently disrupted traffic flow.

stories.title: Rawalpindi court sends anchorperson Rabia Ahsan's husband on one-day physical remand
summary: A Rawalpindi court on Monday remanded Ahsan Tahir, the husband of television anchorperson Rabia Ahsan, in police custody for one day in connection with her murder and directed police to produce him before the court again on Tuesday.

The case was registered at the police station on the complaint of Rabia's brother, Khurram Ahmed, who accused Ahsan of shooting his sister at their home in Gulshanabad Sector II, on Adiala Road, on Sunday.
Read: Anchorperson shot dead at home in Rawalpindi, husband arrested Rabia had presented her last programme on a mainstream television channel on Saturday night.

stories.title: Bangladesh force draw in second Test
summary: Towhid Hridoy made history with a record-breaking match aggregate of 324 runs as Bangladesh fought back to force a draw in the second Test against West Indies on Monday, handing the visitors a 1-0 series victory.
Hridoy was the standout performer for Bangladesh, following his unbeaten 242 in the first innings with 82 in the second to become the first Bangladeshi batter to score 324 runs in a Test match.
His unbeaten double-century helped Bangladesh recover from 88-3 to post 386, earning them a 30-run first-innings lead over West Indies' 356.

stories.title: Rs18 billion sought for resolving financial issues of KP varsities
summary: PESHAWAR: The provincial higher education department has sought a grant of Rs18 billion from the federal government to resolve financial issues of most of the public sector universities in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
The letter stated that 26 of the 34 universities in the province were in financial deficit.
The higher education department has demanded a three-part grant of Rs18.0 billion for clearing the accumulated deficits, outstanding liabilities, development and seed money for endowment funds.

stories.title: Israel, US negotiating new multiyear military aid agreement: report
summary: Israel and the United States are negotiating a new multiyear military aid agreement, Israeli newspaper Yedioth Ahronoth reported Monday.
Yedioth Ahronoth said US military aid to Israel “will not end immediately,” contrary to previous remarks by Trump.
Israeli negotiating teams were stunned by Trump’s announcement that US military assistance to Israel will end by the close of 2026 and were initially unsure what he meant, the newspaper said.
